title: Start at 25 or at 35?

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: Sam, my friends keep saying they'll start investing once they earn more.

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: Here's why waiting is expensive. Take two people who each put away 300 dollars a month.

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: Ana starts at 25. Ben starts at 35. Both stop at 65, and both earn an average of 7 percent a year.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: So Ana just has ten more years of saving.

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: Ten more years, and only 36,000 dollars more out of her pocket: 144,000 in total against Ben's 108,000.

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: But at 65, Ana has about 787,000 dollars. Ben has about 366,000.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: She ends up with more than double, from a quarter more money?

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: That's compounding. The returns start earning returns, and the early years have the longest to grow.

sentences.speaker: spk_1
sentences.text: So the cheapest thing you can buy is time. Start small, start now, and raise it when you earn more.
